transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Leah (CSM), Marta (CTO, LatticeAI), Jamal (Infra), Hannah (Security), Raj (ML Eng), Tess (Product)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you say name and role?
[00:06] Marta (LatticeAI CTO): Marta, CTO. Thanks.
[00:08] Jamal (LatticeAI Infra): Jamal, infra lead.
[00:09] Hannah (Security): Hannah from security.
[00:11] Raj (ML Eng): Raj, ML engineering.
[00:13] Tess (Product): Tess, product.
[00:15] Samir: Awesome. Quick agenda: we want to scope the private network POC, confirm residency regions, nail down egress constraints, and finalize a benchmark plan with success criteria and timeline. Priya will run through the technical checklist.

[02:02] Priya (Redwood SE): Thanks. Very quickly — two deployment flavors we typically see: VPC peering (classic) and AWS PrivateLink / Private Service Connect patterns. For peering we need route exchange and cross-account peering, for PrivateLink we give you an endpoint service and you create an ENI — slightly different security posture.
[02:28] Jamal: A couple of questions: we run strict egress controls — outbound only through our corporate NAT with static IPs. Can Redwood accommodate static egress allowlisting?
[02:36] Priya: Yes. We can run Private (on-prem or VPC) with egress through your NAT. For hosted we have fixed egress ranges per region; for Dedicated/Private we can annotate the NAT IPs or run peering so traffic never traverses public internet. There was a slight hiccup earlier where the doc called it Red wood Dedicated, but we mean Redwood Dedicated.
[03:01] Hannah: For compliance we need KMS integration and audit logs; also SOC2 and pen test summaries. We might need the HSM option.
[03:12] Leah (CSM): We'll attach SOC2; HSM is an enterprise add-on, we can scope it.

[04:05] Raj: For the actual workloads — two profiles: interactive chat (low token per request, 256 tokens avg, target p99 latency) and batch embeddings (large throughput, 8k text pieces/day). We need numbers to size the pool.
[04:28] Priya: Got it. For interactive: what's your concurrency target?
[04:33] Tess: We're planning for 50 concurrent active users during peak, but requests translate to about 50 RPS sustained with spikes to 80 for short periods.
[04:41] Priya: Good. For batch: Raj, you mentioned 8k texts/day — are those heavy and long?
[04:48] Raj: Each text is ~200–400 tokens average; embedding model chosen is a 2.7B open model variant. We want to quantify embeddings/sec. We're OK with quantized models if quality stays within our baseline.

[06:10] Diego (Redwood SE): A practical benchmarking plan: we'll run three tests — interactive latency profile (50 RPS, with burst to 80, measure p50/p95/p99), sustained throughput for batch embedding (concurrency tuned to hit max throughput), and failure/recovery (simulate AZ loss). We'll provide k6 scripts and a harness container.
[06:35] Marta: The p99 target we discussed internally is 300–400ms, anything above 500ms is risky for UX.
[06:42] Priya: For the model and infra combos we'll give options: hosted with regional constraint, dedicated nodes in your region, or private deployment. Each has different network surface area and cost.

[08:05] Jamal: On the networking side: our constraints — we must keep egress within EU region, no traffic leaving eu-west-1 and all egress IPs must be allowlisted. Also we have a SOC requirement that logs are kept for 1 year and we need audit log streaming to our SIEM.
[08:25] Leah: Redwood Console supports token-level logs and export hooks; we can stream events to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export. We'll include retention options.
[08:40] Hannah: SAML SSO, RBAC and admin roles too. We need role separation so devs can't pull raw data.
[08:48] Samir: We'll map RBAC roles in the Console for the POC.

[09:50] Priya: On VPC peering vs PrivateLink pros/cons — peering is simpler routing but requires cross-account routing and can expose full route table; PrivateLink is more controlled (endpoint-level), better for tight egress rules and doesn't require route propagation. Downsides: PrivateLink has per-ENI IP usage and slightly higher operational steps.
[10:20] Jamal: Which one reduces public egress most?
[10:23] Priya: Both can avoid public egress if configured properly; PrivateLink tends to be easier to ensure no public path because connections stay inside AWS networking with an endpoint. Peering can leak if route tables are misconfigured.

[11:30] Raj: For benchmarks — what's realistic for embeddings with a quantized 2.7B on your Dedicated pool?
[11:38] Diego: Preliminary: with quantized 4-bit and good batching we expect ~900–1300 embeddings/sec on a 8-GPU cluster depending on batch size and seq lengths. We'll test batch sizes 8/16/32 and measure tokens/sec and GPU utilization.
[11:55] Raj: Good. For interactive we need to test KV cache warm vs cold; for chat we care about tail latency (p99) when cache miss happens.
[12:04] Priya: We'll include prefix cache warmups. Also we'll run tests with and without continuous batching to show latency/cost tradeoffs.

[13:30] Marta: About region locking — can we force inference to only run in eu-west-1 for the POC?
[13:35] Samir: Yes. For Dedicated/Private we can pin nodes to eu-west-1. For hosted we can limit to regional endpoints; we'll provide a region policy.
[13:47] Hannah: And if we need an on-prem air-gapped later, is that a separate engagement?
[13:51] Leah: Yes, that's a Private On-Prem package. For POC we can simulate strict residency with Dedicated nodes in your region.

[15:02] Tess: Timeline check — what are the milestones?
[15:07] Priya: Proposed: customer sends network details and CIDRs by 11/10; Redwood provides benchmark harness by 11/11; test window 11/18–11/21 for initial run; review and remediation week of 11/24; decision on rollout by early December.
[15:25] Jamal: That aligns with our quarter planning. We need firewall change windows — will coordinate.

[16:40] Samir: Success criteria idea (we can iterate):
 - Interactive: p99 < 350ms for single-turn responses at 50 RPS sustained, error rate < 0.5%
 - Batch embeddings: sustained throughput >= 1,000 embeddings/sec for the 2.7B quantized model with quality delta <= 0.5% vs baseline (we'll capture eval set)
 - Network: all traffic for the POC is contained in eu-west-1, egress only via allowlisted static IPs
 - Security: KMS integration enabled and SOC2 docs delivered

[18:00] Hannah: We will provide an evaluation prompt set for quality delta calculation and a baseline embedding similarity metric to compare quality.
[18:10] Priya: Great. We'll take those and add them to the harness.

[19:05] Raj: What about cost signals — can you give rough cost per 1k embeddings or per 1k tokens for the Dedicated config so we can model?
[19:13] Samir: We can provide ballpark unit economics after we pick the exact node type and quantization. For now we'll provide a cost-per-hour per node and an estimated token-per-second curve.
[19:30] Diego: Also note the Optimize recommendations: batching/caching settings that balance latency and cost. We'll include suggested profiles in the report.

[20:22] Marta: Any blockers we should raise now? Network approvals are the gating item.
[20:27] Jamal: Yes, we need network security review signoff and firewall ACL windows.
[20:31] Leah: We'll provide a one-pager for your security and network teams summarizing required ports (HTTPS, 443 outbound to PrivateLink or peering IPs), expected CIDRs, and sample routing tables.

[22:05] Priya: Regarding test artifacts — we'll send: k6 load scripts, dockerized harness, a small eval dataset for embeddings, and a template results sheet for you to fill in.
[22:18] Raj: Can we run a smoke benchmark on a smaller window before the full window? 
[22:22] Priya: Yes, we'll do a smoke test to validate connectivity and basic latency. Recommend 30 minutes of low RPS first.

[23:40] Tess: On legal — any special contract for the POC?
[23:45] Samir: Standard POC MSA with a short addendum for Dedicated resources; pricing for the POC itself is usually covered by Redwood for initial tests, but longer Dedicated capacity during pilot may be quoted. We'll loop in legal if needed.

[25:00] Marta: I want to emphasize: we cannot allow any data to leave the EU for these workloads. That is non-negotiable.
[25:07] Samir: Understood — we'll treat that as a hard requirement.

[26:30] Jamal: Operational question: how do you surface audit logs? We want parity with our existing SIEM fields.
[26:36] Leah: We can export logs in JSON with timestamp/user/request id fields, and deliver via S3 sink or syslog forwarder. We'll map fields and sample format in the doc.

[28:15] Diego: Failure tests: we'll simulate AZ failure and simulate increased cold-starts to observe p99 spikes. Also we'll run a distortion test with synthetic network latency to see sensitivity.
[28:32] Raj: Good. Also test cache invalidation behavior; make sure replays don't cause duplicate charges.

[30:40] Priya: Action plan recap: 1) Jamal provides CIDRs/egress IPs/allowed regions by 11/10. 2) Redwood (Priya/Diego) provides harness + scripts by 11/11. 3) Smoke test week of 11/17, main run 11/18–11/21. 4) Deliver report and cost estimates by 11/25. 5) Security artifacts (SOC2, KMS options) by 11/14.
[31:05] Samir: Anything else?
[31:10] Hannah: Please include contact for escalation during test windows.
[31:13] Samir: We'll include on-call and CSM contact.

[33:00] Marta: Ok thanks everyone. One quick note — we might want PrivateLink to start because our platform team is nervous about any peering changes.
[33:08] Priya: We'll include PrivateLink first-run instructions and peering as fallback.

[34:45] Raj: Minor: ensure the harness tags requests so we can attribute traffic to the right client id for billing reconciliation.
[34:52] Diego: We'll add client_id and request_id tags in the output.

[36:00] Tess: If Redwood can share similar case study (anonymized) about a eu-only POC that would help expedite internal approvals.
[36:08] Leah: We have a short case study; will share after redaction.

[37:20] Samir: Final recap and I'll send calendar invites for the smoke window and include network checklist.
[37:30] Marta: Thanks, appreciate it.
[37:33] Jamal: Thanks.
[37:35] Hannah: Thanks.
[37:36] Priya: Thanks everyone.

[48:00] End of recording.
